subject: Dedicated capacity deep-dive: GPU fit, streaming behavior, and validation path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@cobalthealth.com>, Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity deep-dive: GPU fit, streaming behavior, and validation path

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to meet the infra team. High-level recap + proposed validation path below so we can align on scope before the pilot SOW.

Recap of performance targets you gave on the call:
- Customer SLOs we should validate: P95 latency <= 180 ms for interactive streaming flows; streaming chunk latency (P50) < 80 ms; steady-state throughput target ~1,200 tokens/sec with ability to burst 2x for 2–3 minutes.
- Concurrency: ~300 concurrent streams at peak (mostly short-lived requests, 4–6s each).
- Model: two variants — smaller streaming-optimized model for UI interactions (context 2k) and larger LLM for batch rerank/recall (context 8k).

Initial HW fit observations (short form):
- H100 (SXM): best headroom for low-latency streaming (native NVLink KV cache, better small-batch latency). For your concurrency/streaming shape we estimate 2–3 H100 GPUs reserved to hit the 1,200 tokens/sec sustained target with P95 headroom.
- A100 80GB: strong sustained throughput per GPU but higher per-token latency under small-batch streaming; 3–5 A100s required to reach similar sustained throughput, with slightly higher P95.
- L40S / L4-class: cost-effective for embeddings and smaller models, but we'd need many more cards for the larger model footprints — better for non-interactive batch inference.

Key platform levers we'll validate in the pilot:
1) Continuous batching + adaptive batching threshold tuning (to keep streaming latency low).
2) KV/pre-refix caching for conversational flows to reduce tokens/sec compute.
3) Reserved capacity sizing vs. burst policy (how many reserved GPUs to commit vs autoscale).
4) Quantization profile tradeoffs for the large model (fp16 -> int8-ish profiles we recommend).

Proposed next steps:
- We run a 48-hour performance validation window using a small traffic replay you provide (or our traffic generator if you prefer).
- Redwood will provide a GPU-fit matrix with expected tokens/sec, steady-state P95 numbers, and cost delta per hour for each sizing option (attached: cobalt_validation_scope.pdf).
- Finalize pilot SOW (3-week validation + one week analysis).

Would you be able to: (a) confirm the streaming SLO numbers above are correct; (b) share a representative 1-hour traffic capture; (c) confirm NDA / pilot SOW owner so we can route docs?

Attachments: cobalt_validation_scope.pdf (scope & test plan)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the detailed recap. A few clarifications before we move to a pilot SOW.

Questions:
1) Cost delta: can you provide a rough $/hour delta between the "H100 reserved" vs "A100 reserved" options in the matrix? We need to budget this in our procurement review.
2) Burst behavior: our product can do short bursts up to 2–3 minutes but we need sub-200ms P95 even during bursts. How does reserved capacity + burst autoscale interact? If autoscale spins up extra nodes, do we see temporary latency spikes?
3) Prefix/KV caching: will that materially reduce GPU count for the conversational model? If so, by how much do you estimate?

We can provide a 1-hour traffic replay (anonymized) by end of day Friday (our infra team needs to scrub identifiers). We are happy to run a 48-hour window but need the test to include a 60-minute high-burst interval to validate P95 under load.

Also: please include an architecture diagram + SOC2 evidence page in the pilot materials — procurement will ask.

Thanks,
Anika Rao

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity deep-dive: GPU fit, streaming behavior, and validation path

Anika — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers then an actionable test plan proposal.

Short answers:
- Cost delta: ballpark (list price comps, will refine in matrix): H100 reserved pod ~ $25–35/hr (per reserved node equivalent we recommend), A100 reserved pod ~ $12–18/hr. Exact depends on cloud SKU and tenancy; we'll include hourly math in the matrix (attached: redwood_gpu_fit_matrix.xlsx).
- Burst behavior: autoscale will spin new nodes; we configure routing so that new nodes are only used for additional throughput (not mid-stream handoffs). You will see a short tail in latency while new nodes warm KV cache, so we recommend a small reserved headroom to cover burst ramps (we suggest 20% above steady-state target).
- Prefix / KV caching: yes — for conversational flows we typically see 25–40% reduction in compute for repeated contexts. For your workload I'd estimate a ~30% effective reduction in tokens/sec compute for the interactive model, which translates into ~20–30% fewer GPUs required compared to an uncached baseline. We'll validate during the pilot.

Proposed validation/test plan (we can finalize in the SOW):
1) Duration: 48 hours (including one scheduled 60-minute high-burst period you requested).
2) Test environment: Dedicated Redwood Private cluster in us-west (VPC peered) with reserved capacity as follows:
   - Option A (latency-first): 3x H100 reserved GPUs, 1x H100 burst pool (autoscale up to +2).
   - Option B (throughput-first): 6x A100 reserved GPUs, autoscale +3 A100 for bursts.
   - Option C (cost-min): 10x L40-class GPUs reserved (for non-streaming batch + embeddings), separate streaming staging on H100s for UI flows.
3) Metrics we will capture: tokens/sec (ingress/egress), P50/P95/P99 latency per stream, cold-start latencies for autoscale events, GPU utilization, and cost/hour.
4) Deliverables: perf matrix, recommended reserved config for SLO compliance, and runbook of tuning knobs (batching thresholds, prefetch/kvcache settings).

Next actions for us to start:
- You send 1-hour anonymized replay (or give permission for Redwood to synthesize if that's faster).
- Approve which sizing options you want tested (we can run all three but that increases runtime).
- Sign pilot SOW (we'll send a one-page pilot SOW after you confirm scope).

Attachments: redwood_gpu_fit_matrix.xlsx (preliminary sizing & cost math). I'm looping in Tessa (solutions eng) and Karthik (performance lead) to coordinate the run and entitlements.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
